classification.difficultyReason: Model projection lengths geometrically and maximise the resulting sums on a restricted angular domain.

content.prompt: In the figure below, $\angle AOB=\frac\pi3$. The point $P$ moves such that $OP=10$ and $\angle AOP=\theta$, where $0\le\theta\le\frac\pi3$. $M$ and $N$ are points on $OA$ and $OB$ respectively such that $PM\perp OA$ and $PN\perp OB$.

spec.description: Unshaded planar angle with OA horizontal, OB at 60 degrees, an interior illustrative P, perpendicular feet M and N, OP, two distinct angle arcs and all six point labels.
spec.mathematics: N is the orthogonal projection of P onto OB and M onto OA. The illustrative position of P does not specify a numerical value of theta. All diagram distances are drawing coordinates, not additional givens.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry and labels are permanent question givens; no solution result is shown.

answer.short:
$10\sqrt3$.

The projection sum is $10\sqrt3\cos\left(\theta-\frac\pi6\right)$, maximised at $\theta=\frac\pi6$.
answer.worked:
Right-triangle projections give $OM=10\cos\theta$ and $ON=10\cos\left(\frac\pi3-\theta\right)$.
$$\begin{align*}OM+ON&=10\cos\theta+10\cos\left(\frac\pi3-\theta\right)\\OM+ON&=15\cos\theta+5\sqrt3\sin\theta.\end{align*}$$
Matching $R\cos(\theta-\alpha)$ gives $R\cos\alpha=15$ and $R\sin\alpha=5\sqrt3$, so $R=10\sqrt3$ and $\alpha=\frac\pi6$.
$$OM+ON=10\sqrt3\cos\left(\theta-\frac\pi6\right).$$
At $\theta=\frac\pi6$, which lies in the permitted interval, the cosine is $1$. The maximum is $10\sqrt3$.

answer.short:
$10$.

The perpendicular-distance sum is $10\cos\left(\theta-\frac\pi6\right)$, maximised at $\theta=\frac\pi6$.
answer.worked:
Right-triangle projections give $PN=10\sin\left(\frac\pi3-\theta\right)$ and $PM=10\sin\theta$.
$$\begin{align*}PN+PM&=10\sin\left(\frac\pi3-\theta\right)+10\sin\theta\\PN+PM&=5\sqrt3\cos\theta+5\sin\theta.\end{align*}$$
Matching $R\cos(\theta-\alpha)$ gives $R\cos\alpha=5\sqrt3$ and $R\sin\alpha=5$, so $R=10$ and $\alpha=\frac\pi6$.
$$PN+PM=10\cos\left(\theta-\frac\pi6\right).$$
The cosine reaches $1$ at the permitted value $\theta=\frac\pi6$, so the maximum is $10$.
